comments.text:
In my state of Indiana, there are rules for selling chickens. A quick overview:

In Indiana, you can sell up to 20,000 birds per year from your own raising under state and federal processing exemptions regulated by the Indiana State Board of Animal Health (BOAH). The rules change depending on your total volume: 

Volume Tiers and Rules

Fewer than 1,000 birds per year:

No state permit is required from BOAH.

You must sell directly to the end consumer (on the farm, via delivery, or at farmers' markets/roadside stands).

Meat sold at markets must be frozen, while on-farm sales can be refrigerated or frozen.

1,000 to 20,000 birds per year:

Requires a Limited Permit from the Indiana State Board of Animal Health.

Sales are restricted to direct-to-consumer channels, or specific local retail/restaurant/hotel (HRI) avenues depending on the exact permit type.

Over 20,000 birds per year:

Requires full, daily state or federal (USDA) inspection oversight.

General Requirements for Exempt Sales

Raised by You: The birds must have been raised on your premises.

Labeling: Packages must include proper labels featuring the product name, net weight, farm name/address, packing date, and an explanatory statement that the facility is exempt from standard inspection.

No Wholesale to Stores: Uninspected small-scale sales cannot go to grocery stores or third-party commercial distributors for resale.

I show this because i use to purchase pastured chicken meat from a small farm. They were running low on chicken near the end of the selling season. When explaining why they were low, they said that they were only allowed to sell 1,000 chickens a year.
Now i raise my own. 😅
